KEY FINDING (the survey's headline, flagged for groom, body intent preserved rather than silently rewritten): the body's ac3 asks money to round-trip 'updates through 9999999999.99' (10 integer digits). That value CANNOT round-trip on the merged contract. Verified on-tree at main 3211717: AMOUNT_MAX = Decimal('999999999.99') in app/schemas/expense.py:41, app/schemas/budget.py:33, app/services/expense_service.py:46, app/services/budget_service.py:61, with sa.Numeric(12,2) columns. Chapter 5 5.11.2 is the authoritative per-layer statement (Database NUMERIC(12,2); Pydantic condecimal(max_digits=12, decimal_places=2)) and supports the merged capacity; Chapter 7 7.10.1's 'Max value 9999999999.99' (and Chapter 8's parseFloat(v) <= 9999999999.99 FE snippet) is internally inconsistent with its own max_digits=12 - 10 integer digits need NUMERIC(14,2). Chapter 12 12.5.2 says only 'Amount: Positive, max 12 digits, 2 decimals' and Chapter 2 2.4.4 / Chapter 12's threat tables say only 'Decimal everywhere, NUMERIC(12,2)' - i.e. both chapters support the merged capacity, and NO chapter besides 7.10.1/8 states the 1e10 number. Suggested resolution direction (pinned in ac3, direction only; groom ratifies): round-trip through AMOUNT_MAX itself ('999999999.99') and pin '9999999999.99' as the over-max 422 INVALID_AMOUNT field 'amount' case, which matches the already-merged-and-indexed t13 ac2 / t14 ac2 over-max behaviour ('10000000000.00' -> 422 INVALID_AMOUNT). This is a spec-vs-merged-contract contradiction, NOT a production bug: no production change is warranted and changing AMOUNT_MAX would re-open the merged t13/t14 contracts (out of t15's scope per W16). The ac3 checkbox now carries an inline [AMENDED at survey ...] note pointing at the Notes section so the original intent (top-of-range coverage) stays visible.
